solution:
The chapter states it directly: "The President appoints the election commissioners. The Chief Election Commissioner cannot be removed from his post easily or on account of any political reasons." So the answer is (a) President.

The chapter gives the reason behind that removal protection — to preserve the independence of the Election Commission — which is precisely why appointment does not rest with the Prime Minister, the head of the governing party. The Speaker of the Loksabha and the Vice President are not mentioned in this chapter at all.

The chapter states it verbatim: "Sukumar Sen was the first chief election commissioner after independence." It adds that he was given charge after the Election Commission was established in 1950. So the answer is (c) Sukumar Sen.

None of the other three names appears anywhere in this chapter. They are recognisable enough to tempt a guess from outside the book, but the chapter names Sen outright and links no one else to the post.

The chapter assigns the task explicitly: "Creating constituencies is the responsibility of the Delimitation Commission. The Delimitation Commission does not succumb to any pressure while restructuring the constituencies." So the answer is (b) Delimitation. The chapter's own list of the stages of an election also opens with the establishment of constituencies, which corroborates it.

The nearest rival is 'Timetable', because deciding the timetable and programme of elections is indeed one of the functions the chapter lists — but that function settles when an election is held, not how constituencies are drawn. Scrutiny of candidates' applications is likewise done by the Commission itself and there is no selection committee; actual voting appears only as a stage in the election process, not as a committee.

[Note: the question describes the body as a committee of the Election Commission, whereas the chapter presents the Delimitation Commission as a body in its own right and never as a sub-committee of the Election Commission. The keyed option is unaffected.]
